A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedMVP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Matching content across renumbering and relocation supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FedMVP classification experiments, generalization benchmarks, ablations, and qualitative analyses, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a comparison of prompting locations in Table A9.

M1.justification: The proposed PromptFormer architecture, attribute conditioning, losses, aggregation, inference scoring, and conditional LoRA tuning remain unchanged. Table A9 evaluates alternative prompting configurations without revising the proposed FedMVP procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same dataset and task coverage, including base-to-new, domain, cross-dataset, and non-federated evaluations. The new prompting comparison uses existing generalization settings.

E2.justification: Table A9 adds textual and dual-encoder prompting variants as explicit comparators to FedMVP's visual prompting. Existing named benchmark baselines, including FedVPT and DESC, retain their participation.

E3.justification: The new Table A9 comparison varies whether multimodal prompts enter the text encoder, both encoders, or the vision encoder. Previously stated splits, metrics, shots, participation rates, and communication budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused ablation testing prompt insertion location across base-to-new, MSST, and SSMT settings. Existing component, client-participation, client-size, shot-count, hyperparameter, LLM, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added ablation continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table A9 adds textual-prompting scores of 73.56/66.26/65.89 and dual-encoder scores of 75.95/69.14/68.76 for B2N/MSST/SSMT, alongside retained visual-prompting scores of 78.27/73.02/72.63. Numerical results in corresponding pre-existing tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The non-IID assumptions, mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(9), and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical content. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about multimodal contextual conditioning and improved generalization remain. v2 repeats the existing introduction's 1.57%–2.26% advantage in the abstract and conclusion; this does not establish a stronger claim.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly hypothesizes that dual-encoder prompting is redundant when prompts already contain multimodal information, attributes poorer textual prompting to overfitting, and explains the computational benefit of caching text representations.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code-release promise with an explicit repository link. Section 4.1 also clarifies that local accuracy uses the converged server model on clients; this disclosure does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on sigmoid-loss pretraining, robust fine-tuning, dual-modality prompting, and the PACS dataset, while removing works including Florence and latent diffusion. These are limited contextual changes; FedTPG remains the closest prior method.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the abstract and several related-work, method, result, and conclusion paragraphs, standardizes terminology, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. The narrative and section hierarchy remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A9, relocates the DESC comparison and Figure 10, and rearranges existing main-text plots. Table labels and captions receive edits, while the existing diagrams, plots, and principal table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides focused evidence for choosing visual-only prompting, adds its interpretation, and replaces a code-release promise with concrete access information. Clearer prose and citation corrections also help. These are limited gains: the method and main results remain unchanged, and the new ablation lacks detailed configuration and uncertainty reporting.
